prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on what you mean by shadow work and what kind of spiritual practice you want (Jungian inner work vs. trauma‑informed parts work vs. meditation/nondual practice, etc.). Below I’ve grouped reputable online options by approach, with short notes on who each suits and safety tips so you can choose what fits you.

If you want a quicker personalized list, tell me: your goals, prior experience, budget, and whether you have a history of trauma or mental-health concerns.

A. Shadow work (psychological / Jungian-style)
- Jung Platform — hosts multiple courses, workshops and live webinars on shadow integration taught by Jungian analysts and authors. Good for theory + guided exercises and a Jungian orientation.
- The Shift Network (shadow-work programs) — runs multiweek courses and summits on shadow integration led by established authors/teachers (often experiential). Quality varies by instructor but many include structured practices and group integration.
- Udemy / Skillshare (select courses) — many practical “shadow work” classes (journaling prompts, inner child exercises). Cheap and practical but variable quality — read reviews and sample previews.

Who these fit: people wanting Jungian language, archetypal frameworks, or structured group programs. Caution: shadow work can bring up strong emotions — prefer trauma‑informed teachers or a therapist if you have a trauma history.

B. Parts‑work and trauma‑informed inner work
- IFS Institute (Internal Family Systems) — official trainings and many introductory resources by Richard Schwartz and colleagues. IFS is highly practical for working with “inner parts” (what many call shadow aspects).
- Somatic/trauma-informed courses — look for trainings from reputable clinicians (e.g., SE trainings, trauma‑informed integration courses). These are often professional-level but some introductory workshops are available online.

Who these fit: people wanting a clinical/therapeutic, evidence-informed approach to integrating difficult parts or trauma. Highly recommended if prior trauma exists.

C. Meditation, mindfulness and foundational spiritual practices
- UMass Center for Mindfulness — MBSR (Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction) online programs (well established, evidence-based).
- Palouse Mindfulness — free online MBSR-style course (self‑paced). Good for beginners.
- Waking Up (Sam Harris), 10% Happier, Headspace, Insight Timer — apps/courses for meditation, mindfulness, and short courses on concentration, insight, and compassion.
- Sounds True — hosts courses and multiweek programs by teachers such as Adyashanti, Jack Kornfield, Tara Brach (meditation and spiritual practice).

Who these fit: people who want steadier, safety-first practices that help stabilize the nervous system before deeper shadow work.

D. Nondual / direct spirituality (ego and “shadow” from a spiritual lens)
- Courses and satsangs from teachers like Adyashanti, Rupert Spira, Eckhart Tolle (available via Sounds True, their own sites or platforms). These explore awakening, presence, and often how the “ego” (and its darker sides) disidentify with true nature.

Who these fit: people focused on awakening/nondual insight rather than psychological integration. Can be destabilizing if done without support.

E. Practical & lower-cost starter options
- Insight Timer — many free guided meditations and short courses on inner work.
- Udemy — cheap starter courses (read reviews).
- Free resources: journaling prompts, shadow‑work worksheets (many teachers/blogs offer free material).

How to choose and what to watch for
- Decide your aim: therapeutic integration vs. spiritual awakening vs. practical emotional regulation. Different courses serve different aims.
- Trauma history: choose trauma‑informed instructors or work alongside a therapist if you have PTSD, complex trauma, or significant emotional dysregulation.
- Format preferences: live group + teacher feedback vs. self‑paced videos; group support can be very helpful for shadow work.
- Credentials & reviews: check teacher background (clinical training if offering trauma work), read past-student reviews, and see if there’s a refund policy.
- Start gently: combine meditation/mindfulness and somatic grounding before doing intense shadow inquiries. Keep a plan for support if difficult material arises (therapist, coach, trusted friend).

If you want, I can:
- Recommend 3–5 specific courses tailored to your budget and goals (therapeutic vs. spiritual vs. hybrid).
- Suggest a 8–12 week learning path (practices + journaling + safety measures) you can follow at home.

Which direction are you most drawn to (Jungian shadow work, IFS/parts work, mindfulness + stabilization, or nondual spiritual practice)?
